claim: For every nonempty finite set V of distinct integers at least 4 with sum_{d in V}1/(d-1)=1 and containing a multiplicatively independent pair, H_V(x)>x holds for every real x>1, where p_d(x) is the least nonnegative integer power of d at least x and H_V(x)=sum_{d in V}(p_d(x)-1)/(d-1).

quadruple.stage: Exact geometric prefix sums of finitely many labelled integer-power streams, using ordinary integer and real arithmetic.

The negative side is one finite V and a failing scale, with an integer witness available from accepted CP28 Section9. shape.target_quantity: A yes/no strict inequality property with exact target H_V(x)>x, not an optimal numerical constant or a density upper bound. An analytical proof without a useful explicit global threshold suffices, but a mere unspecified eventual range would not establish all x>1.
